statements.statement: console.log("42") and console.log(42) produce the same type of value in TypeScript.
statements.explanation: They look the same on screen, but "42" is a string (text) while 42 is a number. TypeScript treats them as completely different types.

statements.statement: Numbers in console.log do not need to be wrapped in quotes.
statements.explanation: Numbers go directly into console.log without quotes. Adding quotes would make them strings instead of numbers.
Decimal numbers like 3.14 can be passed directly to console.log just like whole numbers.
